subject: protected variable names / scoping problem in geom_boxplot

messages.author: ed1059ade83f0afe
messages.subject: protected variable names / scoping problem in geom_boxplot
parts:
hi,

not sure whether this warrants a bug report, so here goes:

it seems that lexical scoping errors can occur if you are unlucky enough to have column names
in your data that are also used as names for objects in some internal calculations:

e.g.:
##############
## generate some artifical data
d <- expand.grid(n = c(5, 10), snr = c(2, 5), alg = 1:3,
    index = factor(rep(1:5, 10)))
d <- cbind(d, y = rnorm(nrow(d)))

basic <- ggplot(d, aes(index, y)) + facet_grid(n ~
    snr)
basic + geom_jitter(aes(col = factor(alg)))
#works

basic + geom_boxplot(aes(index, y, fill = factor(alg)))
#fails - warnings() shows a problem with statements including 'n'
#    may also fail with other _geoms that do internal calculations involving a local variable 'n'

## rename 'n' to 'N':
d$N <- d$n
ggplot(d, aes(index, y)) + facet_grid(N ~ snr) + geom_boxplot(aes(index,
    y, fill = factor(alg)))
## works --> seems like 'n' should somehow be a protected variable name in this case?
##############

anybody else ever had that problem or a similar one?
i really don't get the proto-stuff used in ggplot2 so I don't know how to fix this
(other than renaming my variables, see above...)

P.S:
> options(warn = 2)
> basic + geom_boxplot(aes(index, y, fill = factor(alg)))
> traceback(max = 10)
[....]
28: within(df, {
        xmin <- xmin + width/n * (seq_len(n) - 1) - diff * (n - 1)/(2 *
            n)
        xmax <- xmin + d_width/n
        x <- (xmin + xmax)/2
    })
27: strategy(df, width = width)
[....]

so the the offending code is in a function strategy() [which is invisible via ggplot2:::strategy :( ]
